newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Harradine sees Telstra mandate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Harradine sees Telstra mandate.

text.p: Key Australian Independent Senator Brian Harradine said on Thursday the government had a mandate to partially privatise telecoms carrier Telstra Corp and that it was not his role to obstruct such a policy.
"I do not see my role, nor do I see the Senate's role, to be obstructionist of government policy for which they've got a mandate at the election," Harradine told reporters.

The government needs the support of Harradine and another Independent, Mal Colston, if parliament is to pass its bill to sell Telstra. Colston also said earlier on Thursday that the government had a mandate for the sale.
Harradine, who has not yet expressly said he will vote for the bill, earlier revealed an agreement with the government that implies his ultimate support.
He and the government have agreed to seek a delayed commencement of the bill while a committee examines redeemable preference shares as an alternative to a sale of equity.
The government also announced on Thursday two initiatives to answer the requirements of the Independents.

Both had expressed concerns about job losses outside of the main cities if Telsta were privatised, and the government responded by promising a A$250 million fund -- paid out of the privatisation proceeds -- to develop rural telecoms infrastructure.
The government also enlarged its promised environmental repair fund to A$1.1 billion from A$1.0 billion and promised that it would assist Harradine's home state of Tasmania.
The Independents also backed the government in the necessary intermediate votes for the bill on Thursday.
The government had hoped for a final vote on the bill on Thursday, but the Senate will not now complete it until at least Monday.
The partial privatisation of Telstra is expected to raise about A$8 billion.
